The request could not be submitted with the provided fields. When
`error.field` is present, it uses the submitted JSON path so the
frontend can show the message next to the matching form input.

Standard error response. Validation errors include `error.field` when

highlight the corresponding input.

FilmCountryAvailability.description: Country availability lists for external form display. Empty arrays mean no restriction from that list. Submit is still validated server-side.

FilmScreeningRequestBaseInput.description:
Fields submitted by a custom Film Screening Request form. The endpoint
validates required fields by scenario:
Theatrical requests require `venue.venue_slug`; non-theatrical
in-person requests require requester-supplied location fields; instant
submissions require ticketing details; and Events On Demand™
submissions require threshold data.
`screening.start_date` plus `screening.start_time` must be in the
future. Required threshold deadlines must also be in the future and
before the Screening date.
Non-instant submissions may omit `ticketing` because the Host adds or
finalizes ticket tier(s) on GATHR before publishing. Theatrical On
Demand® submissions omit client-provided `threshold` because GATHR
derives the Theatrical On Demand® deadline and threshold server-side
from native Screening cost/deadline rules.

experience.description:
Screening experience. `tod` is Theatrical On Demand®, `buyout` is
theatrical buyout, `standard` is standard ticketing, and `eod` is
Events On Demand™.

preferred_subtitle_guid.description: Optional subtitle choice for non-theatrical in-person Screening Requests. Use a subtitle `guid` returned by the config endpoint, or null/empty for no subtitles.

availability_windows.description:
Screening date windows by Screening type. There is no hybrid window:
hybrid requests are validated against `non_theatrical`.

FilmScreeningRequestEstimate.description:
Informational fee preview for external rendering. This payload includes
structured, non-HTML fee rows and guidance text derived server-side from
native fee messaging. Treat this as a preview, not final settlement.

line_items.description:
Display-ready estimate rows. Render `label` and `amount` directly in
your UI response.

next_steps.description: Ordered instructional steps parsed from estimate messaging.

notes.description: Additional estimate notes safe for external display.

payment_required.description: Indicates whether the GATHR-managed completion step may require payment.

FilmScreeningRequestEstimateFeeDetails.description:
Structured fee-rule metadata for machine use and user-facing explanation.
Use `fee_type` to determine which optional fields are relevant.

fee.description:
Fee value associated with `fee_type`:
- `flat_fee`: flat amount
- `per_person`: per-person amount
- `share_of_ticket_sales`: percentage value

fee_terms.description: Human-readable fee explanation suitable for end users.

minimum_guarantee.description: Estimate-time minimum guarantee value, if configured.

FilmScreeningRequestEstimateInput.description:
Optional pricing preview input. For theatrical estimates, include
`venue_slug`, `screening_start_date`, and `screening_start_time` so the
estimate can validate Venue availability before returning pricing.

experience.description:
Screening experience. `tod` is Theatrical On Demand®, `buyout` is
theatrical buyout, `standard` is standard ticketing, and `eod` is
Events On Demand™.

host_type_id.description: A Host type ID returned by the config endpoint.

paid_event.description: Whether tickets are paid. On-demand experiences are treated as paid for estimates.

screening_start_date.description: Required for theatrical estimates. Use YYYY-MM-DD.

screening_start_time.description: Required for theatrical estimates. Use 24-hour HH:MM local Venue time.

tickets_sold.description: Current or expected tickets sold for estimate display.

FilmScreeningRequestLegal.description:
Legal policy links and the required terms checkbox copy for external
Screening Request forms. Integrations must display `terms_checkbox_html`
near the terms acceptance checkbox before submission.

terms_checkbox_html.description:
Renderable HTML matching GATHR event and rental checkout terms
checkbox copy. Displaying this copy is required before collecting
terms acceptance.
terms_checkbox_html.example: I agree to GATHR's Terms of Use and have read and acknowledged GATHR's Privacy Practices.

accepted.description: Must be true. External forms must display the config endpoint's `legal.terms_checkbox_html` before collecting acceptance.

FilmScreeningRequestSubmission.description:
Creates a GATHR Screening Request and sends the requester an email to
continue in GATHR. Submit does not create Events or Bookings and does
not publish anything.

FilmScreeningRequestSubmissionResult.description:
Submit success response. `screening_request.next_step` is the frontend
instruction; show the returned `message` and direct the requester to
check email. `status` is the Screening Request status after the
continuation email is sent.

message.example: Check your email to finish your request.

instant.description: Whether this request follows the instant completion path.

host_description.description: The description of the Host profile.

host_name.description: The name of the Host profile.

host_url.description: The URL for the Host profile.

id.description: The slug for the Host profile.

HostTypeFee.description: Null when no applicable Film fee is configured.

amount.description: Fee amount. Share fees are percentage values.

minimum_guarantee.description: Minimum guarantee amount when configured, otherwise 0.

asks_nonprofit_ein.description:
If true, ask the Host for their nonprofit EIN or tax ID. This is
used for Host types where nonprofit status may affect Screening
review or pricing.

asks_organization.description:
If true, ask the Host for the name of the organization hosting the
Screening, such as a school, company, nonprofit, faith group, or
community organization.

HostTypeScreeningFees.description:
Display fee metadata for this Host type. Fee values reflect the Film's
current configured Film fees, including Host-type-specific fees and the
general Host-type fallback. Use the estimate endpoint for final pricing.

donation_total.description: The total amount donated to Event charities with the Order.

id.description: The unique ID for the Order.

order_date.description: The date and time the Order was placed.

order_total.description: The total amount paid by the person who placed the Order.

ticket_face_value_total.description: The amount paid by the person who placed the Order, without fees and taxes.

user_email.description: The email address of the person who placed the Order.

user_first_name.description: The first name of the person who placed the Order.

user_last_name.description: The last name of the person who placed the Order.

dates_flexible.description: Optional flag indicating whether the requester is flexible on the selected date/time. Defaults to false when omitted.

end_date.description: Required for non-theatrical in-person, virtual, and hybrid Screening Requests when the form collects an end date. Send `end_date` and `end_time` together or omit both.

end_time.description:
Required for non-theatrical in-person, virtual, and hybrid Screening
Requests when the form collects an end time. Use 24-hour `HH:MM`,
zero-padded. Send `end_date` and `end_time` together or omit both;
when supplied, the end must be after the start.

estimated_attendance.description: Optional expected attendance or selected capacity for validation and estimates. Defaults to 0 when omitted.

paid_event.description: Optional paid/free signal. Defaults to false when omitted; TOD/EOD submissions are treated as paid server-side regardless of this value.

start_date.description: Screening start date. Combined with `start_time`, this must resolve to a future date/time.

start_time.description:
Screening start time in 24-hour `HH:MM` format, zero-padded
(`09:00`, not `9:00`). This is the same format the Venue
availability endpoints return. Combined with `start_date`, this must
resolve to a future date/time.

timezone.description: Required for non-theatrical in-person, virtual, and hybrid Screening Requests. Use an IANA timezone name.

host_type_id.description: A Host type ID returned by the config endpoint.

nonprofit_ein.description: Nonprofit EIN or tax ID for the Host, when requested by the selected Host type.

organization.description: Organization name for the Host, when requested by the selected Host type.

ScreeningSubtitleOptions.description:
Optional subtitle choices for non-theatrical in-person Screening
Requests. Integrations should render their own "No subtitles" option;
submit an empty or null `preferred_subtitle_guid` when no subtitles are
selected.

ScreeningThreshold.description:
Threshold/deadline data for on-demand experiences. Required for Events
On Demand™ submissions. Theatrical On Demand® submissions omit
client-provided `threshold` because GATHR derives the Theatrical On
Demand® deadline and threshold server-side from native Screening
cost/deadline rules. Use `attendance` when `type` is `attendance`, or
`revenue` when `type` is `revenue`. `deadline` must be before the
Screening date and must be in the future.

deadline.description: Required on-demand threshold deadline. Must be in the future and before the Screening date.

ScreeningTicketing.description:
Ticketing details for instant Screening submissions. Non-instant
submissions may omit `ticketing` because the Host adds or finalizes
ticket tier(s) on GATHR before publishing. Required nested fields depend
on `mode`: `free_quantity` for free Screenings, `single.title` and
`single.price` for single-tier paid Screenings, or at least one tier
with `title`, `price`, and `quantity` for multi-tier paid Screenings.

date.description: Date to check in YYYY-MM-DD format.

availability.description:
Venue availability for the requested date. The same keys are always
returned, available or not. All times are 24-hour `HH:MM` in the
Venue's local timezone, the same format `screening.start_time` uses
on submit.

available.description: Whether the Venue can be booked on the requested date.

end.description:
Latest bookable time in 24-hour `HH:MM`, Venue-local. Null when
`available` is false.

exceptions.description:
Time-window overrides that apply to the requested date only.
Upcoming date-level exceptions are returned by the weekly
availability endpoint instead, not here.

start.description:
Earliest bookable time in 24-hour `HH:MM`, Venue-local. Null
when `available` is false.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name for every time in this response.

ScreeningVenueDateException.description:
A date-level availability override for the Venue, returned by the weekly
availability endpoint.

available.description:
Whether the override makes the date available. An entry with
`available: false` is a blackout — disable that date even when its
weekday is open.

deposit_percentage.description: Venue deposit percentage for the date.

fee.description: Venue rental fee for the date.

non_refundable.description: Whether the Venue deposit for the date is non-refundable.

ScreeningVenueDateTimeException.description: A time-window availability override for the requested date.

available.description: Whether the override makes that time window available.

deposit_percentage.description: Venue deposit percentage for the window.

fee.description: Venue rental fee for the window.

non_refundable.description: Whether the Venue deposit for the window is non-refundable.

ScreeningVenueInput.description:
Location fields for the Screening. Which fields are required depends on
`screening_type`: theatrical requests send `venue_slug`; non-theatrical
in-person and hybrid requests send the requester-supplied location
fields; virtual requests send an empty object (`{}`). The `venue` key
itself is always required.

address.description: Venue address for non-theatrical in-person and hybrid requests.

capacity.description: Optional capacity for non-theatrical in-person and hybrid requests. When supplied, it must be a non-negative integer.

city.description: Venue city for non-theatrical in-person and hybrid requests.

latitude.description: Venue latitude for non-theatrical in-person and hybrid requests.

longitude.description: Venue longitude for non-theatrical in-person and hybrid requests.

name.description: Venue name for non-theatrical in-person and hybrid requests.

venue_slug.description: Required for theatrical requests using a selected GATHR Venue.

distance_km.description: Distance from the requested latitude/longitude in kilometers.

instant_book.description: Whether the Venue can be booked instantly.

response_time_days.description: Estimated response time in days for non-instant Venue booking requests.

ScreeningVenueWeekdayAvailability.description:
Availability for one weekday. Closed days return `available: false` and
nothing else.

available.description: Whether the Venue is open on this weekday.

end.description:
Window end in 24-hour `HH:MM`, Venue-local. Present only when
`available` is true.

fee.description:
Venue rental fee configured for this weekday, as stored by the
Venue. Present only when `available` is true. This is not the Film
fee: use the estimate endpoint for Screening Request pricing.

start.description:
Window start in 24-hour `HH:MM`, Venue-local. Present only when
`available` is true.

availability.description:
Venue weekly availability for date and time selection. Weekday keys
are ISO-8601 day of week: `"1"` is Monday through `"7"` is Sunday.
There is no `"0"` key.

exceptions.description:
Upcoming date-level availability exceptions for the Venue. Apply
them to those specific dates in the date picker.

min_notice_days.description:
Minimum lead time in days. Disable dates sooner than this many
days from today.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name for every time in this response.

talent_description.description: The description of the Talent profile.

talent_name.description: The name of the Talent profile.

info.description:
Use the GATHR API to access account, profile, order, and Film Screening
request data.

API requests must be made over HTTPS and include your GATHR API key and
account email address.

Film Screening Request API endpoints use a Film-specific publishable API key
from Film Management. Publishable keys are intended for Filmmaker-owned web
forms and must be used from whitelisted domains.

Film Screening Request API endpoints are intended to be called directly from
browser-based Screening Request forms on whitelisted domains.

Enable and configure API access for your Film in Film Management > Film API.
From there, create a publishable Film API key and add the domains that are
allowed to use it.

get.description: Get all of a user's Host and Talent profiles.

Get the public configuration needed to render a custom Screening Request
form for a Film.

Use this endpoint before displaying your form so your integration can
show the current request types, fields, limits, and options available for
the Film.

The response tells the frontend which Screening types and experiences
can be offered, which Host types can be selected, whether fee estimates
are available, what display fees apply to each Host type, what
availability windows apply, and what legal terms copy must be displayed
before submission. Treat this response as the source of truth for form
rendering. Submit and estimate are still validated against current
server state.

Host type options include `asks_organization` and `asks_nonprofit_ein`
so external forms know which extra Host details to collect, plus `fees`
for the Film fees that apply to that Host type.

legal.terms_checkbox_html: I agree to GATHR's Terms of Use and have read and acknowledged GATHR's Privacy Practices.

post.description:
Preview current pricing and request details before submission.

This endpoint is optional and informational. Final pricing and
availability are confirmed during GATHR completion.

Use this endpoint after the requester has selected the fields needed for
an estimate. The endpoint does not create users, Screening Requests,
Events, Bookings, payments, or abandoned attempts. The response can be
displayed as a pricing preview and may be stored again by submit as the
latest estimate for the Screening Request.

Estimate responses include structured, non-HTML fee presentation fields
for frontend rendering:
- `line_items` for row-level display labels and amounts.
- `fee_details` for fee-rule metadata and human-readable `fee_terms`.
- `next_steps` and `notes` for guidance copy.

These fields are derived server-side from native fee messaging and are
safe to render directly. Integrations should not render native
`film_fee_html` directly.

Integration guidance:
- Treat estimate responses as non-binding previews.
- Use `fee_details.fee_type` to decide which fee fields are relevant.
- Do not infer absent fields.
- Use `fee_terms` when explaining fee logic to end users.

get.description:
Search Venues for theatrical Screening Request forms.

This endpoint returns theatrical Venues near the provided latitude and
longitude, or near a server-geocoded `location` such as a city, state,
ZIP/postal code, or other location string.

Provide either `latitude` plus `longitude`, or `location`. When both are
supplied, latitude and longitude are used.

Search results do not include weekly availability. After a requester
selects a Venue, call the weekly availability endpoint to retrieve date
and time selection data.

This endpoint is only part of the theatrical request flow. For
non-theatrical in-person requests, the form submits location details in
the `venue` object instead of selecting a GATHR Venue.

parameters.name: location

parameters.description: Latitude used for location-based search. Provide with longitude, or provide location instead.
parameters.name: latitude

parameters.description: Longitude used for location-based search. Provide with latitude, or provide location instead.
parameters.name: longitude

parameters.description: Search radius in kilometers around the provided latitude/longitude.
parameters.name: radius

post.description:
Check availability for a selected theatrical Venue on a specific date.

Use this endpoint after a requester selects a date so your form can
restrict available times using GATHR availability and exceptions.

`availability` always returns the same keys: `available`, `start`,
`end`, `timezone`, and `exceptions`. `start` and `end` are 24-hour
`HH:MM` times in the Venue's local timezone and bound the time picker
for that date; they are `null` when `available` is false. `exceptions`
contains only the time-window overrides that apply to the requested
date. Upcoming date-level exceptions are returned by the weekly
availability endpoint instead.

Submit `screening.start_time` in the same 24-hour `HH:MM` format.

This helps the frontend avoid invalid times before submit. The submit
endpoint rechecks Venue availability server-side, so the frontend should
still handle `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses for `screening.start_date` or
`screening.start_time`.

parameters.description: The Venue slug returned by Venue search.
parameters.name: venue_slug

availableDate.description:
`start` and `end` bound the time picker. Entries in
`exceptions` with `available: false` are blocked ranges
inside that window — exclude those times; `available: true`
entries are informational and never widen or narrow the
window.
availableDate.summary: Venue is open on the requested date

unavailableDate.description:
The response keeps its full shape when the Venue is closed.
Offer no times for the date.
unavailableDate.summary: Venue is closed on the requested date

200.description: Venue availability for the date returned.

post.summary: Get Venue availability on a date

get.description:
Get weekly availability for a selected theatrical Venue.

Use this endpoint after a requester selects a Venue from search results
so your form can render date and time selection using GATHR availability.

The response identifies the selected Venue and returns availability data
used to constrain date/time UI. Call the date-specific availability
endpoint after the requester picks a date.

`availability` is keyed by ISO-8601 day of week: `"1"` is Monday through
`"7"` is Sunday. There is no `"0"` key. Each day has `available`, plus
`start` and `end` as 24-hour `HH:MM` times in the Venue's local
`timezone` when the Venue is open that day. `exceptions` lists upcoming
date-level overrides, and `min_notice_days` is the minimum lead time in
days.

parameters.description: The Venue slug returned by Venue search.
parameters.name: venue_slug

weeklyAvailability.description:
Day keys are ISO-8601 (`"1"` Monday through `"7"` Sunday).
Closed days carry only `available: false`. All times are
24-hour `HH:MM` in the Venue's local `timezone`.
weeklyAvailability.summary: Weekday windows with an upcoming exception

post.description:
Submit a custom Film Screening Request form.

This endpoint creates or finds the requester user, ensures a Host
profile exists, creates a GATHR Screening Request, stores the submitted
payload and latest estimate, creates an email continuation token, and
sends the requester a GATHR email.

This endpoint does not create an Event or Booking, and it does not
publish anything. Instant requests and any requests that require payment
continue through the emailed GATHR status page. External forms do not
collect payment details and the Film API does not expose payment
endpoints. Non-instant requests continue to GATHR confirmation before
offer or approval workflows.

After a successful submission, show the requester the returned `message`.
The next frontend action is always `screening_request.next_step` with a
value of `check_email`. If payment is required, GATHR handles it on the
emailed status page after submission. Unconfirmed Screening Requests may
expire if the requester does not continue within GATHR's configured
submission window.

GATHR validates the current Film API configuration, requester fields,
email deliverability, Host type, terms acceptance, Film availability,
geographic restrictions, selected Screening experience, Venue/location
fields, theatrical Venue availability, instant ticketing/capacity fields,
future start date/time, threshold/deadline fields, and subtitle selection
server-side.

Required field scenarios:
- All submit requests require `screening_type`, `experience`,
  `requester`, `screening`, `venue`, and `terms.accepted` with a value
  of `true`.
- `screening.start_date` and `screening.start_time` must resolve to a
  future Screening start date/time.
- Theatrical requests require `venue.venue_slug`. The selected Venue must
  be a valid theatrical GATHR Venue and available for
  `screening.start_date` and `screening.start_time`.
- Non-theatrical in-person requests require `venue.name`,
  `venue.address`, `venue.city`, `venue.latitude`, `venue.longitude`,
  and `screening.timezone`. `venue.capacity` is optional; when supplied,
  it must be a non-negative integer.
- `screening.estimated_attendance` is optional and defaults to `0`.
- `screening.dates_flexible` is optional and defaults to `false`.
- `screening.paid_event` is optional and defaults to `false`; TOD/EOD
  submissions are treated as paid server-side even when omitted.
- Server-calculated instant submissions require `ticketing`.
  Non-instant submissions may omit `ticketing` because the Host adds or
  finalizes ticket tier(s) on GATHR before the Screening can publish.
- When `ticketing.mode` is `free`, `ticketing.free_quantity` is required.
- When `ticketing.mode` is `single`, `ticketing.single.title` and
  `ticketing.single.price` are required.
- When `ticketing.mode` is `multiple`, at least one tier with `title`,
  `price`, and `quantity` is required.
- Events On Demand™ submissions require `threshold.type`, `threshold.deadline`,
  `threshold.estimated_capacity`, and either `threshold.attendance` or
  `threshold.revenue` depending on `threshold.type`. Required
  `threshold.deadline` values must be in the future and before the
  Screening date.
- Theatrical On Demand® submissions omit client-provided `threshold`;
  GATHR derives the Theatrical On Demand® deadline and threshold
  server-side from native Screening cost/deadline rules.
- `preferred_subtitle_guid` is optional and only valid for
  non-theatrical in-person requests when the config endpoint returns
  subtitle options. Use null or an empty string for no subtitles.
- Virtual submit does not require physical venue/location fields. Send
  `venue` as an empty object (`{}`); the `venue` key itself is still
  required. `screening.timezone` is required.
- Hybrid submit requires non-theatrical in-person location fields
  (`venue.name`, `venue.address`, `venue.city`, `venue.latitude`,
  `venue.longitude`) and `screening.timezone`, and is available only
  when the Film enables both non-theatrical in-person and virtual
  Screening Requests.
- Virtual and hybrid Screening date windows: virtual requests use the
  config's `availability_windows.virtual`; hybrid requests use
  `availability_windows.non_theatrical`. There is no separate hybrid
  window.

hybridStandard.description:
A non-instant hybrid Screening: the audience attends in person
and online at the same time. Hybrid submit uses the same
in-person location fields as a non-theatrical in-person
request plus `screening.timezone`, and requires the Film to
enable both non-theatrical in-person and virtual Screening
Requests. Hybrid Screening dates use the non-theatrical
availability window. Ticketing details are omitted because the
Host adds or finalizes ticket tier(s) on GATHR before
publishing.

nonTheatricalFree.description:
A non-theatrical in-person Screening at a requester-supplied
location with free admission. If the selected Film resolves as
instant, include `ticketing` details.

nonTheatricalPaidWithSubtitles.description:
A non-instant non-theatrical in-person EOD Screening using
requester location details and a subtitle GUID returned by the
config endpoint. Ticketing details are omitted because the
Host adds or finalizes ticket tier(s) on GATHR before
publishing. EOD threshold/deadline details are supplied because
EOD does not currently derive them server-side.
nonTheatricalPaidWithSubtitles.summary: Non-theatrical paid multi-tier request with subtitles

theatricalBuyout.description:
A theatrical buyout request. No threshold object is needed
because buyout is not an on-demand threshold experience.
If the selected Film/Venue resolves as instant, include
`ticketing` details.

theatricalTodPaid.description:
A non-instant theatrical on-demand request using a selected
GATHR Venue. Ticketing and threshold details are omitted
because the Host adds or finalizes ticket tier(s) on GATHR
before publishing, and GATHR derives the TOD deadline and
threshold server-side.

virtualStandard.description:
A non-instant virtual Screening streamed online. `venue` is
required but stays an empty object because there is no
physical location, and `screening.timezone` is required.
Ticketing details are omitted because the Host adds or
finalizes ticket tier(s) on GATHR before publishing. Do not
collect streaming links, platforms, or credentials: GATHR
arranges virtual delivery with the Host after confirmation.

tags.description:
Build custom Film Screening Request forms that continue through GATHR by email.

Enable and configure API access for your Film in Film Management > Film API.
Use the publishable Film API key for your custom Screening Request form.
Add the form website's domain to the Film API whitelist.

Recommended frontend flow:
1. Call the config endpoint before rendering the form.
2. For theatrical requests, search Venues, load weekly availability for the
   selected Venue, then check the selected date before allowing time
   selection.
3. Optionally call the estimate endpoint before submit to show current
   pricing information.
4. Submit the request.
5. On success, show the returned message and tell the requester to check
   email. GATHR manages the continuation step.

Treat structured response fields as source of truth. Do not infer missing
fee rules, and do not present estimate responses as final settlement
outcomes.

Submitting the form creates a GATHR Screening Request. It does not create
an Event or Booking, and it does not publish anything. Instant requests
and any requests that require payment continue through the emailed GATHR
status page. External forms do not collect payment details and the Film API
does not expose payment endpoints. Non-instant requests continue to GATHR
confirmation by email before offer/approval workflows.

Validation errors return `error.field` using the same dotted path as the
submitted JSON field, so frontends can map errors back to inputs such as
`requester.email`, `venue.venue_slug`, `ticketing.single.price`, or
`threshold.deadline`.
